title: AI for Everyday HR
summary: Use AI to draft, organise and improve everyday HR work while checking accuracy and keeping sensitive employee information protected.
modules: Map repetitive work and separate drafting support from decisions that need a person.
Create a prioritised HR task shortlist
Write and verify a useful brief
Practise with fictional employee scenarios, source documents and a clear review checklist.
Produce a checked HR communication draft
Document approved inputs, review responsibilities and the point at which work stops for help.
Leave with a reusable AI task playbook

title: People Operations Workflow Automation
summary: Turn a repetitive people-service request into a clear workflow with ownership, approvals and a reliable handover when automation cannot help.
modules: Map a fictional HR request from intake to resolution and identify duplicate handling.
Specify triggers, validation, routing and human approval without exposing personal records.
Walk through missing information, duplicate requests and failed handovers.

title: Digital Onboarding & Employee Journeys
summary: Create an onboarding experience that connects HR, managers and IT, using technology to make responsibilities and the next step clear.
modules: Map the first 90 days from the employee perspective using a fictional starter scenario.
Define tasks, owners, dependencies and useful reminders across HR, managers and IT.
Test accessibility, late starts and missed tasks, then choose feedback points.

title: HR Data Quality & Connected Records
summary: Make people data usable before adding AI. Practise checking fictional HR records, defining ownership and fixing the causes of poor data.
modules: Identify core fields, authoritative systems and the purpose of each data item.
Use synthetic records to detect duplicates, missing values and conflicting definitions.
Define validation, access, correction and reconciliation responsibilities.

title: AI-Assisted Recruitment Operations
summary: Improve recruitment coordination, role briefs and candidate communications with AI, while keeping selection decisions with accountable people.
modules: Map scheduling, briefing and communication tasks that can benefit from assistance.
Identify an appropriate recruitment support workflow
Check AI-generated role requirements and candidate messages against a fictional approved brief.
Produce a reviewed role brief and message set
Test unsupported claims and inconsistent wording; define human review and escalation.
Create a recruitment AI review checklist

title: HR Knowledge & Employee Self-Service
summary: Prepare a trustworthy HR knowledge base and design an assistant that answers from approved sources and hands sensitive questions to a person.
modules: Organise sample guidance by employee intent, content owner and review date.
Write source-backed answers and define what to do when guidance is absent or conflicting.
Challenge the assistant with ambiguous questions, stale sources and requests for private information.

title: People Analytics for Better HR Decisions
summary: Turn a people question into a defensible analysis using synthetic data, consistent metrics and a clear explanation of uncertainty.
modules: Translate an HR business question into measures, definitions and an appropriate comparison.
Explore fictional workforce patterns, missing data and the difference between association and cause.
Prepare a metric definition and evidence table
Explain limitations, avoid identifying small groups and propose a testable next step.
Produce a decision-ready people insight brief

title: Employee Listening with AI
summary: Use AI to organise fictional employee feedback into useful themes without losing nuance or presenting generated interpretations as facts.
modules: Choose questions, participation measures and appropriate boundaries for feedback use.
Compare summaries with synthetic comments and look for omitted or overgeneralised viewpoints.
Prioritise improvements, assign owners and explain how progress will be shared.

title: HRIS Selection & Connected People Systems
summary: Define what your HR systems must do, evaluate them through practical scenarios and plan reliable data handovers between services.
modules: Translate employee journeys into requirements and separate essential capabilities from preferences.
Create a prioritised HRIS requirements brief
Build a vendor demonstration scorecard using realistic onboarding, reporting and access scenarios.
Map field ownership, failure recovery and reconciliation between a fictional HRIS and adjacent tools.

title: Skills Mapping & Technology-Enabled Workforce Planning
summary: Build a practical view of skills and future work, using AI to support exploration while keeping skill claims grounded in evidence.
modules: Break a business scenario into tasks, capabilities and observable evidence.
Review fictional skills records and distinguish verified evidence from self-reported or inferred skills.
Produce an evidence-labelled skills gap map
Compare development, redeployment and recruitment scenarios with explicit assumptions.
Build a workforce development action plan

title: Learning Operations & AI-Enabled Development
summary: Connect learning needs, course design, delivery and evidence so development programmes support a measurable change in work.
modules: Turn a fictional team challenge into observable learning outcomes and a baseline.
Combine AI-assisted drafts, practice, live support and human-reviewed assessment.
Specify completion evidence, reviewer responsibilities and follow-up measures.
Produce a learning operations measurement plan

title: Redesigning HR Services with AI Agents
summary: Design a bounded HR agent that can progress work, use approved records and return reviewable outputs, with clear permissions and recovery steps.
modules: Choose a fictional people-service workflow and specify the agent goal, inputs and allowed actions.
Write an HR agent service brief
Set approval points, permission boundaries, duplicate protection and a human handover.
Test success, refusal, incomplete data and interrupted runs against observable acceptance criteria.
Produce an agent pilot evaluation plan

title: HR Transformation Strategy & Roadmap
summary: Shape a practical HR transformation roadmap around employee experience, operating capability and measurable value rather than a list of tools.
modules: Connect business priorities to the current employee experience and HR operating constraints.
Write a transformation ambition and baseline
Identify dependencies across data, services, technology and people capability.
Define milestone evidence, decision ownership and a benefits review cadence.

title: Responsible AI Governance for HR Leaders
summary: Establish practical oversight of HR AI use: ownership, evidence, access boundaries and review of consequential decisions by qualified people.
modules: Classify fictional HR AI proposals by purpose, information involved and potential employee impact.
Create an HR AI use-case inventory
Specify who approves a pilot, what evidence is required and when specialist advice is needed.
Build an HR AI oversight matrix
Plan quality monitoring, employee feedback, incident handling and stop conditions.

title: Leading People Change in an AI Workplace
summary: Lead the people side of AI adoption with clear communication, participation and support as tasks, skills and working practices change.
modules: Map the impact of a fictional technology rollout on tasks, confidence and manager responsibilities.
Create a stakeholder and change-impact map
Design employee involvement, manager conversations and realistic capability support.
Produce a participation and communication plan
Separate tool activity from better work and create feedback-driven checkpoints.
Build an adoption and adjustment scorecard

title: HR Technology Investment & Value
summary: Challenge an HR technology business case using realistic costs, operational dependencies and evidence that employee services are improving.
modules: Define the problem, alternatives and baseline before choosing a product.
Estimate scenario costs, capacity effects and implementation dependencies without counting benefits twice.
Set pilot criteria, ownership and decision gates for continuing, changing or stopping investment.
Build a benefits and decision-gate plan
